chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Increase in saying Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, and Allahu Akbar, for indeed they will come on the Day of Resurrection with them preceders, followers, and rear-guards, and they are the enduring good deeds.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but God

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting the four Tasbih phrases on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Thawab al-Amal*, linking the Prophet’s instruction to the Quranic concept of 'al-Baqiyat al-Salihat' (enduring good deeds) to emphasize the perpetual spiritual value of these four phrases. The mention of 'muqaddimat' (predecessors), 'mu'akhkhirat' (followers), and 'mu'aqqibat' (rear-guards) reflects the Shia exegetical tradition that these dhikr phrases are personified or accompanied by angels who intercede for the believer on the Day of Resurrection.
